item.title: Help: New writer who wants to create a canon.
item.content:encoded:
Alright, so I'm not exactly new to the SCP community, I've been a lurker for a while but never posted anything. But I have had this idea for a canon, in which a young man discovers that his estranged father is actually the creator/cause of a fair number of anomalies. For example (may or may not appear in future tales/skips) he was annoyed by a coworker and turned him into 106. But the problem is I'm not entirely sure how to make the canon work. I'm much more used to writing non-scp sci fi, so, I guess my main question is. Does it have to be a mix of tales and skips (like pitch-haven) or can it just be tales?

item.title: Re: Incorporeal mass at the center of the Earth
item.content:encoded:
I like the suggestion of using neutrinos, as they seem to be the closest real-world equivalent to 'incorporeal energy'. As for the fading intangibility I am considering a concept of 'neutrino diffusion', similar to 'hume diffusion' in SCP-3001 and SCP-4903, wherein the intangibility is slowly being shared between the incorporeal objects and earths inner core. This would lead to a sudden absence of the inner core, causing a much more disastrous collapse than would happen if the inner core were replaced with corpses. This would also solve the debate of whether the re-materializing object would replace the solid matter or the other way round. What do you think?

item.content:encoded:
Hello SCP Wiki Forums!

I've recently taken an interest in this place when SCP animation videos started showing up in my YouTube feed, particularly ones from the spin-off channel of the Infographics channel. Technically, I've known about the existence of SCPs since around 2014, courtesy of Tumblr, but I've never really thought of actually trying to write stories set in the SCP Universe until now.

Right now, I have a weird idea for an SCP based around the tragedy of Actaeon, that curses those who activate it with Cervocephaly (deer headedness) and causes all dogs nearby to want to kill them, and I'm already starting to think up a narrative for its discovery by the Foundation. It's sort of festive, since it is the time of year for (sleigh pulling) deer after all, and maybe if I'm lucky I'll at least have a draft published in my sandbox before Christmas.

item.content:encoded:
Hey!

My name's Shuu (he/him), I like games and I'm a university student completely unsure of what he's doing with his life!
I've been a lurker of texts here for quite a while actually, but decided that I wanted to give some +1's to all those entries that made me feel stuff (from getting scared of damn text to completely breaking me) because I feel like it's the least I can do for all the good times I've had trying to discover what's each entry about. All the twists and stories behind and how they intertwine with others… So looking forward for more of that, and maybe discussing with people here about it!

And for what thoughts keep me up at night… It's usually whatever I saw last before going to bed. That being the ending of a movie or game (and what happens in the future of that universe, like with FF7). Or sometimes what the cats outside my window are doing.
I swear I can hear them scheming something.

So yeah, glad to be here!

item.title: (Seeking Greenlight) The Ancient Gateway of "Venrensorys"
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights:** Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror/Comedy

Elevator Pitch: An ancient interdimensional gateway with an unknown origin located somewhere in the North Pole area, which leads to a world where lies an entity whose claimed to be a being that has existed longer than existence itself, however, with the attitude of an energetic teenager.

Central Narrative:
SCP-XXXX appears to be an ancient gateway with unknown origin. The gateway is approximately 8,849 meters constructed out of unknown solid materialize and has unknown symbols are written all over it. Any individual who walks into SCP-XXXX would encounter an anomaly whose size is inapplicable to all. The anomaly is designated as SCP-XXXX-01. SCP-XXXX-01 appears to be an inorganic entity with no human facial features, no signs of hair, eyes, nose, mouth, or eyes. Its body is entirely made out of unknown matters presumed it is a type of non-existent dark matter.

SCP-XXXX-01 shows no signs of hostility, shown to have unique knowledge. It would be able to remain patiently/motionless in one place without feeling any urges/aggression over many eternities. However, sometimes it would leave its place1, and will not feel disturbed if any individuals are there to disturb or observed it.

+ show block
– hide block

SCP-XXXX was first discovered when a group of individuals who are exploring the North Pole has reported to the authorities that they'd discovered a mysterious enormous portal while in the middle of finding shelter to avoid an upcoming snowstorm. As this was brought to the Foundation, they've covered it up as fast as possible and deployed a group of agents, MTF-Twilight-10, codename "Broken Stellers," was deployed with the duty is to accompany all of the witnesses out and monitor/guard the area.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This SCP was inspired by a cosmic entity named Venrensorys. But with a few aspects, edit into it.

Additional Notes: So, after watching through SCP-2662, I've decided to come up with this idea.

item.title: Re: Deus Comedenti (Translation: God Eater)
item.content:encoded:
+ show block
– hide block

In other words, it's 'the greater good' theory, but in a way the reader understands the greater good on an immediate level, while also being aware of the sacrifice.

a) I think that's rather disgusting, as that's not actually how the greater good should be considered… for example the wanton sacrifice of individuals within a nation to "avoid spending 12 percent of it's GDP on imports." Not sure how dicey of a moral dilemma you've created here as its on its face, abominable.
b) this is has sorta been done alot on the wiki as well.

The 'God Eater' thing is part of the narrative. It was originally built with the intention to kill ("Eat") gods. With that in mind, it was designed to contain an entity with great power and convert it into raw unthinking energy. It just so happens that it's current users aren't aware of it's designed purpose and utilize it differently.

ok, but my point is that you need to thematically connect the anomaly to the "narrative". For example, if something broke down matter to create energy, I wouldn't assume that was used for killing gods. Typically we don't consider gods to simply be beings of matter. So what I am suggesting is you tweak this anomaly such that it is clear from the anomaly itself that there is something in it that is meant to kill the divine.

As someone fairly interesting in deicide as a narrative device, I am not sure what more you're trying to say. So the thing was meant to kill gods… ok? What thematic core to this anomaly/narrative are you trying to talk about? If its just a thing that which should kill a god… without more, I am not sure how intriguing that will be (not to mention there's plenty of that on the wiki too).

What I think you need to do is stop worrying so much about the plot and start thinking about some themes you could examine through this piece. What are you trying to talk about to the reader?

If its just "this crazy thing exists and oh isn't it a dilemma with a government using it this way" then I still have two problems:
1) the narrative does not seem connected to the anomaly. Why does it kill gods at all? Why would going into the lore of the object connect thematically to the discussion of a callous government willing to sacrifice human lives to save on annual budgets for imports?

2) As it stands, this mostly seems concerned with the discussion of the anomalous properties and the spooky implications of a callous government… but I think to stand out, it needs more. I also think the anomaly itself could be tweaked to differentiate itself from that thing that eats a life and makes energy (you can argue all you want, but why couldn't the government put in ANY organic matter to have the same effect? There's nothing inherently more potent in a human organism than others concerning the conversion of mass into energy.)

item.title: Some edit suggestions
item.content:encoded:
Just going through this article again! I noticed a couple of grammatical mistakes, so I thought I'd suggest them here, along with some other changes. I'm suggesting them here because the article's locked, and I can't make them myself. I am by no means a professional, so I might not always be accurate.

+ Editing suggestions
- This is way longer than I thought it'd be

with David Byrne repeating the line and looking increasingly distraught as hands grip his head.

This line should probably say his hands grip his head, unless the author wanted to imply that there were several disembodied hands present.

Current Status: … Well, heh, looks like… w-was dad really like that? … I need to go lie down… *wimper*

"wimper" should be spelled Whimper.

A Carl Thompson Rainbow Bass. When any song of the band Primus is played, a voice is heard saying "Primus Sucks!"

There should probably be an "on it" after the played.

Item Description: A piece of paper. Descriptions of the item will transform the texts medium into paper.

"Texts" should be spelled with an apostrophe.

Individuals witnessing the resulting effect from this item will feel a strong urge to support the item, usually by compliments.

I feel like the additional "from this item" is unnecessary. The description feels clunkier with that in there. Also, just saying "support" is a little vague for foundation protocol. I think inserting something like "provide the object with emotional support" would make more sense.

that will play any song, with vocals in Kurt Donald Cobain's voice.

The comma there is unnecessary.

Despite the soft appearance,

The "the" should be an its.

will indicate that illegal contraband exist within its conpartments,

The "exist" should be plural.

As much as a small drag of a fingernail along the phone, top to bottom,

This sentence feels very clunky. Removing both commas and inserting "from" before "top to bottom" should help a little.

that show stylized logo of various GoI in

"logo" should be plural.

woman in the painting appear to staring at whoever is loo

Should be "appears" and "be staring"

A white glass plate seven inches in diameter where anything eaten from it is given a strong taste of salt, even if it did not contain any.

This doesn't read Foundation to me at all. I'd suggest rewording the description to something like this: "A white glass plate seven inches in diameter. Any food eaten off of it tastes strongly of salt, even if none was used in its cooking."

A .55 calibre bullet with the date of manufacture as 8/2/1898. The bullet was carbon dated back to 1898 being the only of it's kind created back then. The bullet can be fired an innumerous amount of times.

Same with this one. I'd try changing it to something like "A .55 calibre bullet. Carbon dating suggests it was manufactured in 1898. As no other ammunition manufactured back then matches this object's type, it is assumed to be one of a kind. The bullet can be fired an infinite amount of times without being spent."

That's all I could find for now! I'm fairly new, so if anything I suggested was unwarranted or incorrect, please let me know! Hope this helps.

item.title: Re: Return to Monke - Greenlight Request / Review
item.content:encoded:
Noting that I got a reply in a PM:

GoI format…..holy shit that just might work.

My inspiration for coming to the site and everything and my dream would be to rewrite the GRU-P from the stereotypical Soviet “Red Menace communism bad” standpoint to something more akin to the foundation, albeit with different goals.

Perhaps instead of the language and the other shit I threw in there I could then turn the article into a GoI post or an SCP talking about this GoI that are just monkeys.

The overarching idea I had for GRU-P is that their core tenet being the destruction and absolution of the capitalist chains put upon humans, and I was thinking the Factory could be that personification of capitalism and decay.

and am responding here. Since wikidot doesn't nest PM conversations and I receive a lot of requests each week, it is much more convenient and accessible for me to discuss concepts in a forum thread where the entire discussion is in one place.

If you're intending on writing a completely new GoI, typically a tale would be the easiest way to establish the group. Having a brand new format be the first introduction of such a group may just confuse readers.

I'm not familiar with GRU-P or the Factory, so if you want to pursue those avenues of revision please ask other reviewers who are more experienced with those GoIs for their thoughts.


Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Ideas Critique
Forum thread: Return to Monke - Greenlight Request / Review

As many I liked the concept, but for me there are several things that in the end made it a downvote:

1- The wording problems CannedBread commented on are still all over the place and they're glaring. In a pseudo-scientific article this harms immersion and compound to other issues;

2- For me the containment breach is way over the top (pun intended). Not that I think people shouldn't like over the top breaches (I don't), but in this particular case I think it kinda sidetracks the narrative more than it should. You don't need Hell on Earth here, just a power shortage, and this can be achieved through fairly simpler events;

3- Likewise the triggering event could be made simpler, for similar reasons. All you need is a gas leak into the vacuum chamber (a vacuum chamber that didn't needed to be specially resistant by the way, so its integrity could be another source of embezzlement);

4- I feel that there could be a little more happening in the logs. It is one of the main points of the article and, although it conveys everything it needs to, as a narrative I felt it could be more. Not much, it isn't a question of making it unnecessarily big, just a few more details on the chamber?;

5- You don't need to ascribe to unnecessary harshness in Foundation treatment of other, I do not either, but this level of catastrophic embezzlement certainly would call for something other than wasting further more resources relocating this guy in the larger society (even if as a beggar). I do think highly educated and well trained D-Classes are on short supply.

TL;DR: You need to clean the text and focus your narrative. Do not waste time with big shenanigans that have no bearing with your story. And do not shy from being harsh on someone who caused actual damage.

Personally I would also put a limit on this thing (air resistance should put a practical limit despite continuous torque) and keep the floor a not-so-high temperature to give more space for the log. 200 C° is already quite inhabitable but still explorable.

item.title: Re: Echoes of a Monster
item.content:encoded:
Honestly, the reason Pattern Screamers work (which is debatable imo) is that they're barely described or explained within the SCPs that deal with them…

This feels like although I think a pattern screamer does hate all existence… they don't seem like murderous beings, so much as wanting to erase existence as a concept?

When the scientists are caught, their perspective focuses on one of their five main senses and how the sense is distorted as they become a pattern screamer. Hearing is the only one not mentioned…

ALSO, I don't understand this concept of someone becoming a pattern screamer… which doesn't seem to fit at all. These things are unknowable, pure hatred machines that exist outside of reality.

I just don't think this will add much to the concept. And in terms of having an enjoyable horror story, I don't think this is innovative enough. Again, I don't think that Pattern Screamers fits this sorta story format at all (horror comes out of something and hunts down people in a facility).

item.title: SCP concept-The ring of mimicry
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: its a simple ring that when stored in a container for a given time, it will transform that object into a mimic until taken out. Its containment procedures prevent mimicry by moving it between boxes frequently.

Central Narrative: The ring, while easy to contain, can be catastrophic if not watched after. It does not have a size limit on what it can animate. That means, if given time, the ring could animate the entire facility (key word is given time, it would take decades for the ring to achieve that). Thus the ring has many re-containment procedures and fail-safes to prevent that.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: For this idea, I tried to turn the whole box idea on its head. The whole "if you put it in a box and it stays there, then its safe", I thought about if you put it in a box and then the box tried to kill you, what would it be?

Additional Notes: This is my second idea for an SCP, I'm still very new to this so my clinical tone and ideas may not be satisfactory, I'm open to all critique as I'm here purely to improve.

item.title: Re: The Maw
item.content:encoded:
I think you've got an interesting concept on your hands, but I do feel like it could do with some refining.

+ Spoilers
- Spoilers

Like why exactly is the crash site specifically within 2km of 84"37'02"S 68"32'55"E? Was it just luck that it wasn't in a more populated area? The size of the entity and the amount of biomass at it's disposal makes it seem slightly silly that its only a specific and small crash site without justified reasoning.

The portal seems a bit too 'Avengers 1' with an explosion through a portal into outer space, instantly neutralizing all elements of the skip. It feels like a obvious weak point of the entity that clearly has some form of higher or complex intelligence.

I do look forward to seeing the finished result and I do really like the mix of bodysnatchers, Lovecraft and The Thing going on!
